entries.name: Jim Simons
entries.educationNote: PhD in mathematics, University of California, Berkeley, 1961; undergraduate mathematics degree, MIT, 1958

education.basis: Highest completed qualification: PhD in mathematics, University of California, Berkeley, 1961; undergraduate mathematics degree, MIT, 1958. Professional/master’s degrees score 4; research doctorates 5; bachelor’s degrees 3.

position.basis: Historical career scope: founded Renaissance Technologies (originally Monometrics), led its institutional investment business and retired as CEO in 2010. Leadership of this major investment institution meets the top-institutional-role anchor (5). This is not a current employment claim; Simons died in 2024.

entries.name: Ken Griffin
entries.educationNote: AB with honors in economics, Harvard College, 1989

education.basis: Highest completed qualification: AB with honors in economics, Harvard College, 1989. Professional/master’s degrees score 4; research doctorates 5; bachelor’s degrees 3.

position.basis: Founder and CEO of Citadel and founder/non-executive chairman of Citadel Securities. Citadel reports 3,300 professionals and over $70 billion of client investment capital. Its CEO is the top role of a major financial institution, the position rubric’s 5 anchor. Client assets establish institutional scope, not personal wealth.

education.basis: Highest completed qualification: MBA, Harvard Business School, 1973. Professional/master’s degrees score 4; research doctorates 5; bachelor’s degrees 3.

position.basis: Historical career scope: founded Bridgewater in 1975 and led its development into a global institution as CEO, CIO and chairman. This meets the top-institutional-role anchor (5). He stepped down as CEO in 2017, CIO in summer 2020 and chairman at the end of 2021; this score does not assert current executive authority.

education.basis: Highest completed qualification: JD, Stanford Law School, 1992. Professional/master’s degrees score 4; research doctorates 5; bachelor’s degrees 3.

position.basis: Cofounded PayPal, led it as CEO and took it public; cofounded Palantir Technologies and serves as chairman, according to Founders Fund. These are top corporate leadership roles at major technology institutions, meeting the rubric’s 5 anchor. This assesses scope of authority, not investment success or social benefit.

standing.basis: Navigator/Global Strategy Group national survey, June 4–8, 2026: 8% favorable, 23% unfavorable, 22% don’t know and 46% never heard of Thiel (rounded percentages). Overall favorability below 20% maps to 1 under the displayed rubric. This is favorability, not job approval, and includes respondents unfamiliar with him. Single dated survey; 1,000 base interviews plus oversamples (1,383 total); base margin ±3.1 points.
